high.title: State Bank of Vietnam Applies Special Mechanism for 18 Projects by Vingroup, Sun Group, and Masterise: An Adaptive Response from the Banking System?
high.summary:
The State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) has issued a special credit mechanism for 18 key projects belonging to Vingroup, Sun Group, and Masterise, with total capital requirements exceeding VND 752,000 billion (~USD 29.5 billion). Under this framework, outstanding loans extended to these designated projects will be **excluded from banks' annual credit growth quota (room tín dụng) calculations** — effectively functioning as a form of **targeted credit room expansion**. Participating banks can therefore fund these projects without sacrificing their existing annual credit allocation.

This is a significant macro-prudential development. By carving out exemptions from credit ceiling constraints, the SBV is engineering a **selective loosening of credit conditions** to support large-scale infrastructure and real estate development. However, the article raises a critical secondary concern: even with the credit room obstacle removed, banks must still source the **actual liquidity** to disburse hundreds of trillions of VND. This implies potential upward pressure on deposit rates and interbank funding costs. **Watch for: tightening in interbank liquidity, rising deposit rate competition, and SBV open market operations (OMO) to manage system liquidity.**

---

high.title: Bank Deposit Interest Rates as of June 25 at MB, HDBank, Sacombank, Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank and Others
high.summary: A survey of online deposit rate schedules as of June 25 reveals continued bifurcation between state-owned banks and smaller private lenders. Saigonbank leads the market at 7.2% p.a. for 12-month deposits, while MBV, VCBNeo, PGBank, and VIB all post 7.0% p.a. for the same tenor — meaning five banks now offer 7% or above at the 12-month benchmark. BVBank, LPBank, Bac A Bank, and OCB cluster at 6.9% p.a. for 12 months, with LPBank offering a notable 6.95% for 18-month deposits. The Big 4 state banks (Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank) continue to hold their rates unchanged, maintaining a significant spread below private peers.

high.title: 32 Funds Simultaneously Invest in One Bank Stock Amid Market Volatility
high.summary:
This article reveals significant capital flow dynamics within Vietnamese investment funds during May 2026. According to FiinGroup data, total net fund outflows exceeded VND 2,500 billion in May — a 59.4% surge month-on-month — signaling a defensive shift among institutional investors following the market's historic peak. Equity funds bore the brunt, recording net outflows of over VND 1,800 billion, a staggering 6.8x increase versus April 2026, marking the **31st consecutive month** of net redemptions from equity funds, with cumulative outflows now reaching VND 69,400 billion. Bond funds showed some relief, with net outflows declining 44.7% MoM to VND 742 billion, though this still represents a **9th consecutive month** of net redemptions (cumulative: VND 13,200 billion). ETF outflows surged 159% MoM to nearly VND 1,200 billion. For bond investors, the persistent redemption pressure in bond funds — despite easing — continues to weigh on domestic fixed income demand. The sustained equity fund outflows are a structural bearish signal for the VN-Index. International managers should monitor whether this defensive rotation accelerates into Q3 2026, which could further pressure VND liquidity conditions.

---

high.title: State Bank of Vietnam Issues Urgent Public Advisory on Foreign Currency Transactions
high.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) — specifically its Region 1 Branch — has issued an urgent public advisory warning citizens and businesses about increasingly complex counterfeit foreign currency circulation in the domestic market. The SBV is directing all FX cash transactions to be conducted exclusively through licensed commercial banks, foreign bank branches, or officially registered foreign exchange agents certified by the SBV. The advisory explicitly prohibits peer-to-peer FX cash transactions or exchanges conducted at unauthorized institutions, citing dual risks: exposure to counterfeit currency and legal violations under Vietnamese law (Article 27).

high.title: Fed Chair Delivers Good News for Investors
high.summary:
New Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish stance at his first policy meeting has materially shifted global rate expectations in a direction that could benefit Vietnamese financial markets. The US 10-year Treasury yield has fallen from above 2.5% in mid-May to approximately 2.2% this week — the lowest level in over a year — as Warsh firmly committed to returning inflation to the 2% target and resisted political pressure from President Trump to cut rates prematurely. The decline in US long-end yields, compounded by falling oil prices (retreating to pre-US/Iran conflict levels), reduces the yield differential pressure that has weighed on EM currencies including VND. For VND traders: a sustained decline in USD rates typically eases SBV's intervention burden and reduces capital outflow pressure. For bond investors: lower US yields provide headroom for Vietnamese government bond yields to compress without triggering adverse FX moves. Watch whether SBV uses this window to ease domestic liquidity or defend a stronger VND fixing. The oil price decline is also disinflationary for Vietnam, potentially giving SBV additional policy flexibility.

---

medium.title: Bank Profits Rise 30–50x Over 10 Years: The Fastest-Growing Banks Revealed
medium.summary: A review of Vietnamese bank financial statements from 2015–2025 highlights that the fastest profit growth has come from mid-sized private banks rather than state-owned giants. **SeABank** leads with a ~59x profit increase (from VND 117 billion in 2015 to VND 6,868 billion in 2025), implying a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of approximately 50%. **MSB** follows at 46% CAGR (VND 158 billion → VND 7,058 billion; ~45x growth), and **LPBank** ranks third with pre-tax profit rising from VND 422 billion to VND 14,269 billion. This decade of exceptional profitability in the private banking sector reflects Vietnam's broader credit expansion cycle, improving asset quality management, and fee income diversification. For equity investors in Vietnamese financials, the data underscores the structural outperformance of selective private banks versus state-owned peers, though the current environment of fund outflows and market volatility adds caution to near-term positioning.

medium.title: Bank Deposit Interest Rates on 24/6 at MB, HDBank, Sacombank, Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank...
medium.summary:
A survey of online deposit rate schedules as of June 24 reveals a **continued bifurcation in the Vietnamese deposit rate landscape**. Saigonbank leads the market at **7.2% per annum for 12-month deposits**, followed by MBV, VCBNeo, PGBank, and VIB offering 7.0% p.a. for the same tenor. The majority of banks are clustered in the **6.5%–6.9% p.a. range** for 12-month tenors. This persistent rate differentiation — with smaller and mid-tier banks maintaining notably higher rates than the large state-owned banks — signals ongoing competition for retail deposits. For bond investors, this rate environment suggests **yields on short-to-medium duration government bonds remain under modest upward pressure**, while the broad rate floor appears to be consolidating in the 6.5%–7.2% range. No significant rate cuts appear imminent, particularly given the credit demand dynamics highlighted in the SBV's special mechanism announcement above.

---

medium.title: Latest Forecasts After SJC Gold Bar and Ring Gold Prices Drop by Over VND 15 Million per Tael
medium.summary: SJC gold bars closed at VND 143.2 million/tael (bid) and VND 146.2 million/tael (ask) on June 25, down VND 800,000 from the prior session and more than VND 15 million lower over the past month. The sharp decline tracks a significant global gold selloff, with international spot prices falling over USD 100/oz to approximately USD 3,997/oz — breaking below key support levels at USD 4,100 and USD 4,000, reaching the lowest level since late 2025. Notably, SJC physical bar inventory was reported as sold out, with retail purchases capped at 3 taels of ring gold per customer, though overall transaction demand was described as subdued.

medium.title: Gold Falls 28% from Peak — Experts Weigh In on Long-Term Outlook
medium.summary: Gold spot prices fell over 3% to $3,980.20/oz as the USD index surged to its highest level in over a year, driven by market expectations of Fed rate hikes as early as September 2026, with further tightening possible in December. The CME FedWatch tool reflects growing conviction around tighter U.S. monetary policy aimed at containing inflation pressures. For Vietnam-focused investors, a stronger USD and rising U.S. rate expectations are directly relevant: they typically exert depreciation pressure on the VND, complicate the SBV's FX management posture, and may deter capital inflows into emerging markets including Vietnam. Gold's weakness also has implications for Vietnamese domestic gold market sentiment. Managers should watch whether the SBV responds to USD strength with intervention or rate signaling in coming sessions.

medium.title: Fuel Prices Continue to Fall — Certain Grades Drop Nearly VND 1,700/Litre
medium.summary: Vietnam's Ministry of Finance and Ministry of Industry and Trade jointly reduced domestic fuel prices effective 15:00 on June 25, 2026. E5RON92 petrol fell VND 767/litre to a ceiling of VND 19,359/litre; E10RON95-III dropped VND 837/litre to VND 19,916/litre. Diesel 0.05S saw the sharpest cut at VND 1,668/litre (now VND 21,866/litre), while Mazut fell VND 1,650/kg. Authorities also directed contributions to the Petroleum Price Stabilization Fund at VND 300/litre for biofuels and VND 800/litre-kg for diesel and mazut, without drawing from the fund this round. From an inflation and monetary policy perspective, declining fuel prices reduce near-term CPI pressure, which provides the SBV with additional room to maintain or ease its policy stance — a mild positive for Vietnamese bond yields and rate-sensitive assets.

medium.title: VietBank (VBB) Share Surges Over 11% on Morning of June 26 Ahead of HOSE Listing
medium.summary:
VietBank's (VBB) stock surged more than 11% in the morning session of June 26, reaching VND 13,900/share, bringing its month-to-date gain to approximately 18% and a 58% rally from its mid-March trough. The catalyst is VietBank's approved transfer of listing from UPCoM to the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (HOSE), effective from July 1 (UPCoM trading ceases June 30). Additionally, VietBank will record a shareholder list on June 29 for a 10% stock dividend issuance, part of a broader capital increase program. HOSE approval covers over 1 billion VBB shares. The uplisting is expected to significantly improve liquidity and attract attention from both domestic and international institutional investors, representing a notable addition to the HOSE banking sector index universe.

---

medium.title: BREAKING: US Unexpectedly Strikes Iran Following Hormuz Strait Ship Attack
medium.summary:
The United States launched airstrikes against Iranian missile launch sites, UAV installations, and coastal radar stations on June 26th in retaliation for an Iranian drone attack on a cargo vessel in the Strait of Hormuz. President Trump confirmed the strikes after accusing Iran of violating a ceasefire agreement. This geopolitical escalation carries indirect but meaningful implications for Vietnam: the Strait of Hormuz is critical to global oil transit, and any sustained disruption could reverse the current oil price decline, reigniting inflationary pressures and complicating SBV's monetary policy calculus. Vietnam is a net oil exporter but remains sensitive to global energy price swings through import costs and trade dynamics. Elevated risk-off sentiment from Middle East escalation could also trigger EM capital outflows, putting renewed pressure on VND. Traders should monitor oil price movements and USD/EM dynamics closely in coming sessions.

---

medium.title: LPB Rises Over 10% But Not the Top Gainer — Two Bank Stocks Surge 14% in the Past Week
medium.summary:
The VN-Index posted its second consecutive week of gains, rising 47.38 points (+2.59%) to close at 1,871.91 — the strongest two-week run in recent weeks. However, the rally remained narrow, driven primarily by large-cap names VIC and VHM, while overall market liquidity showed limited improvement. Within the banking sector, 20 stocks advanced versus 7 decliners. Top performers included NVB (+14.29%), KLB (+13.95%), LPB (+10.42%), SGB (+9.24%), and SSB (+8.05%). NVB's surge was linked to its ongoing VND 10,000 billion private placement — one of the largest such issuances in the sector. Notably, the three state-owned banks — VCB, CTG, and BID — all closed in negative territory for the week, alongside EIB (-1.9%) and MBB (-1.0%). The divergence between smaller banks rallying on capital-raising activity and state banks underperforming warrants monitoring, as it may reflect rotation dynamics or liquidity-driven speculation rather than broad-based institutional buying. For equity-focused fund managers, the VN-Index holding above 1,870 is technically constructive, but the lack of broad participation and thin liquidity remain key risk factors.

---

medium.title: Vietcombank Warns Customers: Do Not Click on This SMS Message
medium.summary:
Vietcombank (Vietnam's largest state-owned commercial bank by market capitalization) has issued a public warning regarding a sophisticated SMS phishing campaign impersonating the bank's brand. Fraudsters are mass-distributing text messages containing links to fake Vietcombank websites — notably the domain **vcb-rewards.com** — designed to mimic the bank's official interface. Once a customer clicks the link, the fraudulent page solicits highly sensitive data including phone numbers, cardholder names, card numbers, expiry dates, and CVV codes, enabling near-instant account theft. While this is primarily a cybersecurity and consumer protection issue rather than a macroeconomic event, it is marginally relevant to fund managers with exposure to **Vietcombank (VCB) equity**, as repeated fraud incidents at systemically important banks can attract regulatory scrutiny, generate reputational risk, and potentially weigh on retail banking sentiment. Investors should monitor whether the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) escalates its cybersecurity directives to the broader banking sector.

---
